jp: 日本[にほん]{では|dewa-scope}、一人暮[ひとりぐ]らし{の|no-possessive}人[ひと]{が|ga-subject}増[ふ]え{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: In Japan, the number of people living alone is increasing.
why: Verb stem + つつある describes a change that is under way; ながら cannot be used with ある.

jp: 地球[ちきゅう]{の|no-possessive}気温[きおん]{は|wa-topic}少[すこ]し{ずつ|zutsu-each}上[あ]がり{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: The temperature of the earth is rising little by little.
why: つつある means a change is in progress; the stem 上がり takes つつ, then ある.

jp: 経済[けいざい]{は|wa-topic}ゆっくり回復[かいふく]し{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: The economy is gradually recovering.
why: A process moving toward a new state is expressed with stem + つつある.

jp: 町[まち]{の|no-possessive}様子[ようす]{が|ga-subject}変[か]わり{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: The look of the town is changing.
why: The change has begun and is continuing, which is exactly what stem + つつある says.

jp: 若者[わかもの]{の|no-possessive}間[あいだ]{で|de-scope}この言葉[ことば]{は|wa-topic}広[ひろ]まり{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: Among young people, this word is spreading.
why: A trend that is gradually spreading is described with 広まりつつある.

jp: この町[まち]{の|no-possessive}子[こ]ども{の|no-possessive}数[かず]{は|wa-topic}減[へ]り{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: The number of children in this town is decreasing.
why: Stem 減り + つつある expresses a decline that is currently happening.

jp: 新[あたら]しい技術[ぎじゅつ]{が|ga-subject}社会[しゃかい]{を|o-object}変[か]え{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: New technology is changing society.
why: つつある also follows transitive verbs to say that the change is happening right now.

jp: 状況[じょうきょう]{は|wa-topic}少[すこ]し{ずつ|zutsu-each}良[よ]くなり{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: The situation is gradually getting better.
why: The stem なり plus つつある says the improvement is in progress.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-subject}オンライン{で|de-means}行[おこな]われ{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: Classes are increasingly being held online.
why: A shift toward a new way of doing things is stated with stem + つつある.

jp: この習慣[しゅうかん]{は|wa-topic}消[き]え{つつ|tsutsu-while}あります。
en: This custom is dying out.
why: A gradual disappearance in progress takes 消えつつある.

jp: 景色[けしき]{を|o-object}眺[なが]め{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、ゆっくり歩[ある]きました。
en: I walked slowly while gazing at the scenery.
why: Two actions by one person at the same time: the stem of the side action takes つつ, the main action comes last.

jp: 音楽[おんがく]{を|o-object}聞[き]き{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: I wrote a letter while listening to music.
why: The stem 聞き joins the side action to the main action as simultaneous activities.

jp: 状況[じょうきょう]{を|o-object}見守[みまも]り{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、対応[たいおう]{を|o-object}考[かんが]えます。
en: I will consider how to respond while keeping watch on the situation.
why: Keeping watch and thinking go on together, so the stem of the first verb takes つつ.

jp: 調子[ちょうし]{を|o-object}見[み]{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、仕事[しごと]{を|o-object}進[すす]めましょう。
en: Let's move the work along while keeping an eye on how things go.
why: One person does both things at once, so the stem 見 takes つつ.

jp: 古[ふる]い町[まち]{を|o-object}歩[ある]き{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、歴史[れきし]{を|o-object}学[まな]びました。
en: I learned about history while walking around the old town.
why: Walking and learning happen at the same time, so the stem 歩き takes つつ.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}時々[ときどき]空[そら]{を|o-object}見上[みあ]げ{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、静[しず]かに話[はな]しました。
en: He spoke quietly while now and then looking up at the sky.
why: Looking up is the accompanying action, written with the stem plus つつ.

jp: 自分[じぶん]{の|no-possessive}失敗[しっぱい]{を|o-object}反省[はんせい]し{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、次[つぎ]{の|no-possessive}計画[けいかく]{を|o-object}立[た]てました。
en: I made the next plan while reflecting on my own failure.
why: Reflecting and planning run side by side; the suru-verb stem し takes つつ.

jp: 悪[わる]い{と|to-quote}思[おも]い{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、つい嘘[うそ]{を|o-object}つきました。
en: Although I felt it was wrong, I ended up telling a lie.
why: つつ can join two clashing facts, feeling it is wrong yet doing it, much like "although" in writing.

jp: 無理[むり]だ{と|to-quote}分[わ]かり{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}挑戦[ちょうせん]し続[つづ]けました。
en: Although he knew it was impossible, he kept on trying.
why: Knowing it is hopeless clashes with continuing, which stem + つつ expresses.

jp: 忙[いそが]しい{と|to-quote}言[い]い{つつ/ながら|tsutsu-while}、彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]ジム{に|ni-destination}通[かよ]います。
en: Although she says she is busy, she goes to the gym every day.
why: Saying she is busy and yet going daily contradict each other, which つつ can link.
